title: MZ Help with mz editor on surface pro12

posts.author: Hunter980
posts.body:
Hey everyone,
I'm using a Surface Pro 12 and having some weird problems with RPG Maker MZ. As you can see in the screenshot, my dropdown menus are turning completely black and the editor UI is glitching out.
Downgrading to 1.8 fixes the problem, I would like to use the most updated version if there is a fix.
I've tried rescaling the display and changing the resolution. I've changed about every setting in the emulation settings I could find. I also messed with the dpi settings and connected a external monitor and no luck. I reinstalled windows and rpg maker mz multiple times.
I also used my wife's laptop that has a arm based CPU and the problem is still there. Any suggestions would be great!

Unfortunately that is a wrong assumption and why I asked if the surface is intel-based or not.
I checked since then, and the surface is ARM-Based (Snapdragon), which means it uses an entirely different version of Windows 11 that is only compatible to Intel/Win 11 on the highest API-level.
Any program that was even slightly optimised for Intel/Win is known to have more or less much compatibility problems with ARM/Win, depending on how far it goes into the Intel-optimisations because ARM and Intel have different commands on the processor level.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
KaijuuKimi said:

So what do you think is the culprit as it works fine before but causing this issue in later versions? Because this is out of my expertise, I'll leave it to people who are more knowledgable or had solved this issue.
Click to expand...
You need to understand that x86 architecture - the way CPUs are "built" and "talk" to the OS - is completely different than ARM architecture (what Qualcomm uses in their Snapdragon processors).
x86 is the most common architecture because it was what the very first CPUs for OS-based computing used.
ARM is a newer architecture and as such softwares "communicate" differently with it. It's not as simple as drivers.
Ideally, software needs to be made with ARM in mind. Compatibility layers are going to be hit or miss and likely have high overhead cost (high overhead meaning high CPU utilization)
RM was not built for ARM, so it's going to have problems if running on it.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Hunter980 said:
Hopefully arm will get better compatibility in the future
Click to expand...
unfortunately that is extremely unlikely.
Windows 11 for ARM and Windows 11 for x86 are two different OS, to have GGG make a program for ARM is about the same complexity as making an RPG.Maker for Linux - they basically need to spend months making another version of the maker.
And they won't do that work unless there is a good customer base that would purchase the maker for ARM - which doesn't exist.
That is what we were trying to tell you: your ARM-Operating system may be called Windows, but it is NOT the same Windows as the one for most people. It is rather similar to the "Windows" for mobile phones,,,

posts.body: In most recent computex, Qualcomm already told they are working on to improve the compatibility of arm with x86, and improving the translation layer. Even now the software still run with the problem being only some ui glitch. So it is not something impossible to fix itself in near future.
